panels.rationale: Single histology panel of a surgically removed orbital cavernous hemangioma. The caption and in-text mention describe large anastomosing vascular spaces filled with blood, consistent with the configured orbital cavernous venous malformation and its histologic cavernous spaces finding. No age is stated in the caption or provided in-text mentions.

panels.figure_caption: Large vascular spaces lined by endothelial cells. Note the red blood cells at the periphery of the lumen.
in_text_mentions: in the left eye. Clinical examination revealed alterations of ocular motility and pupil dilation, while imaging suggested the presence of intraorbital hemorrhage. The patient was rushed to surgery on order to decompensate the orbit and protect the optic nerve. An anterior surgical approach was performed through the superior orbital rim allowing entrance to the roof of the orbit and removal of a dark red mass. On histological examination, the lesion proved to be a cavernous hemangioma (Figure 3). Large anastomosing vascular spaces were observed filled with blood and separated by fibrous stroma.
